setup: Feet hip-width, toes behind a line
execution: Swing your arms back as you dip
Throw your arms forward and jump out
Land softly, hips back, knees bent
Stick the landing before you stand
faults: Don't let your knees cave in on landing
Don't fall forward onto your hands

notes: Jump on a non-slip surface with a clear landing zone.
Each jump is a maximal effort. Keep reps low (about 3–5 a set) and rest fully so every jump is fast.
Learn to land before jumping far: practise sticking short jumps first.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the knee, shin or ankle on landing
Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure facing right, with enough room to the right for the jump distance. The figure travels across the frame; the camera stays fixed.

keyPositions.label: Load
keyPositions.describe: Hips back, knees bent, torso leaning forward, arms swung back behind the hips. Heels down.

keyPositions.label: Take-off
keyPositions.describe: Hips, knees and ankles fully straightened, body angled forward about 45°, arms thrown forward and up.

keyPositions.label: Landing
keyPositions.describe: Landed on both feet about a body-length forward. Hips back, knees bent and in line with the toes, arms forward for balance. Held still.

ikHints: Landing feet flat with knees over toes
